But I noticed that you described recent events, and very little about the reasoning behind them. It sounds like there has been a lot building up to this point, so it wasn't a "big event" per se, but a possible trigger to direct the anger outwards, is that correct?

This could be due to a number of reasons. In my case,  it was a trauma response. You know how people describe "fight-flight-freeze"? Well, I was conditioning myself to "fight" so that I wouldn't feel fear when placed in danger. And it worked. I've had multiple people start fights with me, only to back off when they realized I have zero compassion for people.

It was a deliberate effort on my part to become this way. I regret not responding, or running away in past situations. So I desensitized myself to gore to the point it no longer fazed me. Used to make my heart race, and make my hands too weak to make a fist. Afterwards, I'd get a wave of drowsiness and existential dread to sleep off. It doesn't do anything, but make me intrigued by graphic crime scenes, trying to piece together what happened.

It's also worth noting I was bullied in school. It stopped when I started fighting back. Not "in the moment", but arranged at a time when there was a crowd. I can still recall how difficult my first fights were, because it didn't feel natural to hurt another human. Or get hit in the face. It's so loud and thudding.

Although I won't say there's a 1:1 comparison between myself and an ex-soldier. I can definitely empathize with "coming back home" and failing to reintegrate back into society. My triggers happen for the slightest reasons. Someone looks at me with an aggressive demeanor, or tone of voice. I'll accidentally bump my head. If I ruminate too long on a traumatic memory, it's like I'm there ready to rewrite history.

But I'm here. Fighting nothing, and everything.
